reasoning/calendar-clock.text: What was the day of the week on 26th January 1950?
reasoning/calendar-clock.sol: Reference: 1 Jan AD 1 was Monday. Odd days from 1 AD to 1949 = 1949 years. 1949/400 = 4 cycles of 400 years (0 odd days each) + 349 years. 349 years = 264 normal (1 odd day each) + 85 leap (2 odd days each) = 264+170 = 434 odd days ≡ 0 mod 7. Wait, more precisely: every 400 years has 0 odd days. 1600 to 1949 = 349 years. From 1600 to 1949: leap years = 349/4 - century correction. 349/4 = 87 leap years. Century years: 1700,1800,1900 (3 non-leap centuries). So leap years in 1601-1949 = 87-3 = 84. Normal years = 349-84 = 265. Odd days = 265×1 + 84×2 = 265+168 = 433 = 61×7 + 6 ≡ 6 odd days. So 1 Jan 1950 = Monday + 6 = Sunday. Actually, standard reference: 1 Jan 1950 was a Sunday. But the question asks 26 Jan 1950. From 1 Jan to 26 Jan = 25 days ≡ 4 odd days (25 mod 7 = 4). So 26 Jan 1950 = Sunday + 4 = Thursday.

From 28 March 2021 to 28 March 2022: 365 days = 1 odd day. Total odd days = 2. Saturday + 2 = Monday.

quant/number-system.text: If a number 774958A96B is divisible by 8 and 9, then find the value of (A + B).
quant/number-system.sol: For divisibility by 8, last three digits 96B must be divisible by 8. 96B is divisible by 8 when B = 0 or 8. For divisibility by 9, sum of digits must be divisible by 9. Sum = 7+7+4+9+5+8+A+9+6+B = 55+A+B. For A+B, try B=0 => 55+A must be divisible by 9 => A=8 => A+B=8. Try B=8 => 63+A divisible by 9 => A=0 or 9 => A+B=8 or 17. The smallest unique sum is 9.

quant/number-system.text: What is the LCM of (2³ × 3 × 5²) and (2² × 3² × 7)?
quant/number-system.sol: LCM is the product of highest powers of all prime factors. Highest power of 2 = 2³, 3 = 3², 5 = 5², 7 = 7¹. Hence LCM = 2³ × 3² × 5² × 7.

quant/number-system.text: Find the remainder when 2⁴⁵ is divided by 7.
quant/number-system.sol: The cyclicity of 2 mod 7 is 3 (2¹≡2, 2²≡4, 2³≡1). Since 45 = 3×15, we have 2⁴⁵ = (2³)¹⁵ ≡ 1¹⁵ ≡ 1 mod 7. Remainder = 1.

quant/number-system.text: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 360. If one number is 60, find the other.
quant/number-system.sol: For two numbers, Product = HCF × LCM. So 60 × other = 12 × 360 => other = (12 × 360) ÷ 60 = 4320 ÷ 60 = 72.

quant/number-system.text: What is the unit digit of (1234)¹⁰² + (5678)⁵⁸?
quant/number-system.sol: Unit digit depends only on unit digit of base. 4¹⁰²: Cyclicity of 4 is 2 (4¹=4, 4²=16→6, 4³=64→4). Even power → unit digit 6. 8⁵⁸: Cyclicity of 8 is 4 (8¹=8, 8²=64→4, 8³=512→2, 8⁴=4096→6). 58÷4=14 remainder 2 → unit digit 4. So 6+4=10 → unit digit 0. So answer is 0.

quant/percentage.text: If A's salary is 20% less than B's salary, then B's salary is what percent more than A's salary?
quant/percentage.sol: Let B's salary = 100. Then A's = 80. B's salary more than A's = (20/80) × 100 = 25%.

quant/percentage.text: The population of a town increases by 10% annually. If the present population is 1,21,000, what was it two years ago?
quant/percentage.sol: Let P be the population two years ago. After 10% increase each year: P × 1.1 × 1.1 = 121000 => P = 121000 ÷ 1.21 = 100000.

quant/percentage.text: If 60% of (x - y) = 30% of (x + y), then what percent of x is y?
A number is first increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. The net change is:
quant/percentage.sol: Let the number be 100. After 20% increase: 120. After 20% decrease: 120 × 0.8 = 96. Net change = 4% decrease. Formula: a + b + ab/100 = 20 + (-20) + (20×-20)/100 = 0 - 4 = -4%.

quant/percentage.text: In an examination, a student scored 40% marks and failed by 30 marks. Another student scored 50% and got 20 marks more than the passing marks. Find the maximum marks.
quant/percentage.sol: Let max marks = M and passing marks = P. Student 1: 0.4M = P - 30. Student 2: 0.5M = P + 20. Subtracting: 0.1M = 50 => M = 500.

quant/profit-loss.text: A shopkeeper sells an article at a 20% profit. If he had bought it at 10% less and sold it for Rs. 30 more, he would have made a 40% profit. Find the cost price.
quant/profit-loss.sol: Let CP = x. SP = 1.2x. New CP = 0.9x. New SP = 1.2x + 30. New profit = 40% on new CP => 1.2x + 30 = 1.4(0.9x) = 1.26x => 0.06x = 30 => x = 500.

quant/profit-loss.text: Successive discounts of 20% and 10% are equivalent to a single discount of:
quant/profit-loss.sol: Let MP = 100. After 20% discount: 80. After 10% discount on 80: 80×0.9 = 72. Total discount = 28%. Formula: a + b - ab/100 = 20 + 10 - (20×10)/100 = 30 - 2 = 28%.

quant/profit-loss.text: A vendor sells goods at cost price but uses 900 grams instead of 1 kg. His profit percent is:
quant/profit-loss.sol: He pays for 900g but sells as 1000g. CP of 900g = SP of 1000g. Profit = (1000-900)/900 × 100 = 100/9 = 11.11%. Formula: Error/(True value - Error) × 100.

quant/profit-loss.text: A man sold two articles for Rs. 990 each. On one he gained 10% and on the other he lost 10%. Find his overall profit or loss percent.
quant/profit-loss.sol: CP1 = 990/1.1 = 900. CP2 = 990/0.9 = 1100. Total CP = 2000. Total SP = 1980. Loss = 20. Loss% = 20/2000 × 100 = 1%. When SP is same and profit% = loss%, there is always a net loss.

quant/time-work.text: A can do a work in 10 days, B in 15 days. They work together for 4 days, then A leaves. How many more days will B take to finish the remaining work?
A pipe can fill a tank in 12 hours and another can empty it in 20 hours. If both pipes are opened together, how long will it take to fill the tank?
quant/time-work.sol: In 1 hour, fill pipe fills 1/12, empty pipe empties 1/20. Net work = 1/12 - 1/20 = (5-3)/60 = 2/60 = 1/30. Time to fill = 30 hours.

quant/time-work.text: A, B and C can do a work in 20, 30 and 60 days respectively. They work together. A gets Rs. 7200 as his share of wages. Find the total wages.
quant/time-work.sol: Efficiency ratio A:B:C = 1/20:1/30:1/60 = 3:2:1. A's share = (3/6) of total = 7200 => Total = 7200 × 6/3 = 14400. Wait: A's share = 3/(3+2+1) × Total = 3/6 × Total = 7200 => Total = 14400.

quant/time-work.text: A and B together can do a piece of work in 12 days. B and C together can do it in 15 days. A and C together can do it in 20 days. In how many days can A alone complete the work?
A can do a work in 12 days. B is 50% more efficient than A. In how many days can B alone do the same work?
quant/time-work.sol: Efficiency ratio A:B = 100:150 = 2:3. Time is inversely proportional to efficiency. So time taken by B = 12 × 2/3 = 8 days.

quant/speed-distance.sol: Total distance = train length + platform length = 300 + 700 = 1000 m. Time = 50 sec. Speed = 1000/50 = 20 m/s. Convert to km/h: 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h.

quant/speed-distance.sol: Let total distance = 2d. Time for first half = d/30, for second half = d/20. Total time = d/30 + d/20 = (2d+3d)/60 = 5d/60 = d/12. Average speed = 2d ÷ (d/12) = 2d × 12/d = 24 km/h.

quant/speed-distance.text: A thief is spotted by a policeman from 200 m away. The thief runs at 8 km/h and the policeman chases at 10 km/h. How far will the policeman have to run to catch the thief?
quant/speed-distance.sol: Relative speed = 10-8 = 2 km/h = 2×5/18 = 5/9 m/s. Distance to cover = 200 m. Time to catch = 200 ÷ (5/9) = 200 × 9/5 = 360 sec. Distance run by policeman = 10 km/h × 360 sec = (10×5/18) × 360 = (50/18)×360 = 50×20 = 1000 m.

Two circles of radii 5 cm and 3 cm intersect at two points. If the distance between their centres is 4 cm, find the length of the common chord.

For circle 1: 5² = x² + d² where d is distance from center 1 to chord. For circle 2: 3² = x² + (4-d)². Subtracting: 25-9 = d²-(4-d)² => 16 = d²-(16-8d+d²) => 16 = 8d-16 => 8d=32 => d=4. Then x² = 25-16=9 => x=3. Chord length = 6 cm.

quant/geometry-trigo.text: In a ΔABC, if AB = AC and angle B = 50°, find angle A.

ga/indian-history.sol: Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire in 322 BCE with the guidance of Chanakya (Kautilya).

ga/indian-history.text: The famous Battle of Plassey was fought in the year:
ga/indian-history.sol: Battle of Plassey was fought in 1757 between Robert Clive's East India Company and Siraj-ud-Daulah.

ga/indian-history.text: The Indus Valley Civilization is also known as:
ga/indian-history.sol: Indus Valley Civilization is also called the Harappan Civilization after Harappa, the first site discovered in 1921.

ga/indian-history.text: Who was the first Governor-General of independent India?
ga/indian-history.sol: Lord Mountbatten became the first Governor-General of independent India in 1947. C. Rajagopalachari was the last Governor-General.

ga/indian-history.text: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched in:
ga/indian-history.sol: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in 1920 following the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.

ga/indian-polity.text: The Constitution of India was adopted on:
ga/indian-polity.sol: The Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution on 26 November 1949. It came into effect on 26 January 1950.

ga/indian-polity.text: The Rajya Sabha is also known as:
ga/indian-polity.sol: Rajya Sabha is the Council of States, the upper house of Parliament. Lok Sabha is the House of the People.

ga/indian-polity.text: Which Fundamental Right is abolished by the 44th Amendment Act?
ga/indian-polity.sol: The Right to Property (Article 31) was removed from Fundamental Rights by the 44th Amendment, 1978. It is now a legal right under Article 300A.

ga/indian-polity.text: Who appoints the Chief Election Commissioner of India?
ga/indian-polity.sol: The President of India appoints the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners.

ga/indian-polity.text: The Directive Principles of State Policy are enshrined in which part of the Constitution?
ga/indian-polity.sol: DPSPs are in Part IV (Articles 36-51). Part III contains Fundamental Rights.

ga/indian-geography.text: Which is the longest river in India?
ga/indian-geography.sol: The Indus River is the longest river in India at about 3180 km (overall length), though only about 1114 km flows through India.

ga/indian-geography.text: The Western Ghats are also known as:
ga/indian-geography.sol: The Western Ghats are also known as the Sahyadri Mountains. The Eastern Ghats are known as Purvanchal.

ga/indian-geography.text: Which type of climate is experienced in most parts of India?
ga/indian-geography.sol: India experiences a Tropical Monsoon climate, characterized by seasonal reversal of winds.

ga/indian-geography.text: Kharif crops are sown in which season?
ga/indian-geography.sol: Kharif crops (like rice, maize, cotton) are sown with the onset of monsoon (June-July) and harvested in autumn.

ga/indian-geography.text: Which Indian state is the largest producer of bauxite?
ga/indian-geography.sol: Odisha is the largest producer of bauxite in India, followed by Gujarat and Jharkhand.

ga/indian-economy.sol: GDP stands for Gross Domestic Product, the total value of goods and services produced within a country.

ga/indian-economy.text: Who is the ex-officio Chairman of the RBI Central Board?
ga/indian-economy.sol: The Governor of the Reserve Bank of India serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Central Board.

ga/indian-economy.text: The Union Budget is presented by:
ga/indian-economy.sol: The Finance Minister of India presents the Union Budget in the Lok Sabha.

ga/indian-economy.text: Which of the following is a direct tax?
ga/indian-economy.sol: Income Tax is a direct tax (borne by the taxpayer). GST, Excise, and Customs are indirect taxes (passed to consumers).

ga/indian-economy.text: The New Economic Reforms in India were introduced in:
ga/indian-economy.sol: India introduced major economic reforms (LPG - Liberalization, Privatization, Globalization) in 1991 under PM Narasimha Rao and FM Manmohan Singh.

ga/general-science.text: Newton's First Law of Motion is also known as:
ga/general-science.sol: Newton's First Law states that an object remains at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force. This is called the Law of Inertia.

ga/general-science.text: The chemical formula of common salt is:
ga/general-science.sol: Common salt is Sodium Chloride with chemical formula NaCl.

ga/general-science.text: Which vitamin is also known as ascorbic acid?
ga/general-science.sol: Vitamin C is chemically known as ascorbic acid. It is water-soluble and found in citrus fruits.

ga/general-science.text: The human heart has how many chambers?
ga/general-science.sol: The human heart has 4 chambers: two atria (upper) and two ventricles (lower).

ga/general-science.text: Which law states that energy cannot be created or destroyed?
ga/general-science.sol: The First Law of Thermodynamics states that energy can neither be created nor destroyed, only converted from one form to another.

ga/current-affairs.text: Which Indian scheme provides free LPG connections to below poverty line households?
ga/current-affairs.sol: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana provides free LPG connections to BPL households.

ga/current-affairs.text: The highest civilian award of India is:
ga/current-affairs.sol: Bharat Ratna is India's highest civilian award. Padma awards are the next tier.

ga/current-affairs.text: Which Indian wrestler has won two Olympic medals?
ga/current-affairs.sol: Sushil Kumar won bronze in 2008 and silver in 2012, making him the only Indian wrestler with two Olympic medals.

ga/current-affairs.text: The headquarters of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is in:
ga/current-affairs.sol: The IMF's headquarters is in Washington, D.C., USA.

ga/current-affairs.text: Which Indian sports award is the highest for lifetime achievement?
ga/current-affairs.sol: The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award (formerly Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna) is India's highest sporting honour.

english/grammar-basics.text: Identify the part of speech of the underlined word: 'She **quickly** finished her homework.'
english/grammar-basics.sol: 'Quickly' describes the verb 'finished', so it is an adverb of manner.

english/grammar-basics.text: Choose the correct tense: 'I _____ this movie before.'
english/grammar-basics.sol: 'Have seen' is present perfect tense, used for past actions with relevance to the present.

english/grammar-basics.text: Neither the teacher nor the students _____ present.
english/grammar-basics.sol: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Students' is plural, so 'were' is correct.

english/grammar-basics.text: Fill in the blank with the correct article: 'He is _____ honest man.'
english/grammar-basics.sol: 'Honest' begins with a vowel sound (silent 'h'), so 'an' is used.

english/grammar-basics.text: Choose the correct preposition: 'He is addicted _____ smoking.'
english/grammar-basics.sol: The correct preposition with 'addicted' is 'to'. 'Addicted to' is a fixed collocation.

english/vocabulary.sol: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning, kindly, generous. 'Kind' is its closest synonym.
'Ephemeral' means lasting a very short time. 'Eternal' (lasting forever) is its antonym.

english/vocabulary.text: What does the idiom 'Hit the nail on the head' mean?
english/vocabulary.sol: 'Hit the nail on the head' means to be exactly right about something.

english/vocabulary.text: Choose the correct phrasal verb: 'She _____ her father in appearance.'
english/vocabulary.sol: 'Takes after' means to resemble a family member in appearance or character.

english/vocabulary.text: One-word substitution: 'A speech made without preparation'
english/vocabulary.sol: 'Extempore' refers to a speech made without prior preparation.

english/sentence-correction.text: Identify the error: 'The sceneries of Kashmir are very beautiful.'
english/sentence-correction.sol: 'Scenery' is an uncountable noun and has no plural form. It should be 'The scenery of Kashmir is very beautiful.'

english/sentence-correction.text: Improve the sentence: 'I would rather you would leave now.'

options.t: I would rather you leave now.
I would rather you left now.
I would rather you have left now.

english/sentence-correction.sol: After 'would rather', use the base form of the verb (subjunctive). So 'I would rather you leave now' is correct.

english/sentence-correction.text: Arrange the jumbled sentences into a coherent paragraph: P: It has a population of over 20 million. Q: Delhi is the capital of India. R: It is a city with a rich history. S: People from all over the country live here.
english/sentence-correction.sol: Q introduces Delhi, R adds its history, P gives population, S concludes with diversity. So Q-R-P-S.

english/sentence-correction.text: Identify the error: 'One of the boys are playing in the field.'
english/sentence-correction.sol: 'One of the boys' is singular, so the verb should be 'is playing', not 'are playing'.

english/sentence-correction.text: Improve the sentence: 'He is more taller than his brother.'

options.t: He is taller than his brother.
He is more tall than his brother.
He is tallest than his brother.

english/sentence-correction.sol: 'Taller' is already the comparative form. Using 'more' with it is redundant. 'He is taller than his brother' is correct.

english/comprehension.text: Passage: 'The Amazon rainforest produces about 20% of the world's oxygen. It is often called the 'lungs of the Earth'. Deforestation threatens this vital ecosystem, with large areas cleared for agriculture and mining.' What is the main idea of the passage?

options.t: The Amazon is important for oxygen and is under threat
Agriculture is more important than forests
Mining is beneficial for the economy
The Amazon is located in Brazil

english/comprehension.sol: The passage focuses on the Amazon's oxygen production and the threat of deforestation, making option A the main idea.

english/comprehension.text: Passage: 'Sunlight contains ultraviolet (UV) rays that can damage skin. Sunscreen works by absorbing or reflecting these rays. SPF 30 blocks about 97% of UVB rays. However, no sunscreen blocks 100% of UV rays.' What can be inferred from the passage?

options.t: Even with sunscreen, some UV rays reach the skin
UV rays are beneficial for health

english/comprehension.sol: The last sentence states 'no sunscreen blocks 100% of UV rays', implying some UV rays still reach the skin.

english/comprehension.text: Passage: 'The Industrial Revolution began in England in the late 18th century. It transformed economies from agriculture to industry. Key inventions like the steam engine revolutionized transportation and manufacturing.' The word 'revolutionized' in this context most nearly means:
english/comprehension.sol: In context, 'revolutionized' means to bring about a radical or complete change, i.e., 'changed completely'.

english/comprehension.text: Passage: 'Water scarcity is a growing concern worldwide. While 70% of Earth is covered with water, only 2.5% is freshwater, and less than 1% is accessible. Conservation efforts are crucial for sustainable living.' Which of the following is true based on the passage?

options.t: Most of Earth's water is freshwater
Less than 1% of Earth's water is accessible freshwater
Water scarcity is not a serious issue

english/comprehension.sol: The passage states 'less than 1% is accessible', referring to accessible freshwater.

english/comprehension.text: Passage: 'Climate change is primarily caused by greenhouse gas emissions from human activities like burning fossil fuels and deforestation. The effects include rising sea levels, extreme weather events, and loss of biodiversity.' What are the effects of climate change according to the passage?

options.t: Rising sea levels, extreme weather, and biodiversity loss

english/comprehension.sol: The passage clearly states three effects: rising sea levels, extreme weather events, and loss of biodiversity.

english/active-passive.text: Convert to passive voice: 'She writes a letter.'

options.t: A letter is written by her.
A letter was written by her.
A letter is being written by her.
A letter has been written by her.

english/active-passive.sol: Active (simple present): She writes a letter. Passive: A letter is written by her.

english/active-passive.text: Convert to active voice: 'The food was cooked by my mother.'

options.t: My mother is cooking the food.
My mother has cooked the food.

english/active-passive.sol: Passive (simple past): was cooked. Active: My mother cooked the food.

english/active-passive.text: Convert to indirect speech: 'He said, 'I am going to the market.'''

options.t: He said that he was going to the market.
He said that I am going to the market.
He said that he is going to the market.
He said that he went to the market.

english/active-passive.sol: In indirect speech, present continuous ('am going') changes to past continuous ('was going'). Pronoun 'I' changes to 'he'.

english/active-passive.text: Convert to passive voice: 'They will have completed the project by Friday.'

options.t: The project will have been completed by Friday.
The project will be completed by Friday.
The project will have completed by Friday.
The project has been completed by Friday.

english/active-passive.sol: Active (future perfect): will have completed. Passive: will have been + past participle = will have been completed.

english/active-passive.text: Convert to direct speech: 'She asked me if I had seen the movie.'

options.t: She said, 'Have you seen the movie?'
She said, 'Did you see the movie?'
She said, 'Had you seen the movie?'
She said, 'Do you see the movie?'

english/active-passive.sol: Indirect: 'if I had seen' (past perfect). In direct speech, the question was in present perfect: 'Have you seen the movie?'

english/filler-cloze.text: Fill in the blank: 'The committee _____ decided to postpone the meeting.'
english/filler-cloze.sol: 'Committee' is a collective noun treated as singular when acting as a unit. So 'has' is correct.

english/filler-cloze.text: Choose the correct pair of words to fill in the blanks: 'The _____ of the new policy led to _____ among employees.'
english/filler-cloze.sol: 'Implementation' is a noun meaning the process of putting a decision into effect. 'Confusion' is a noun that fits the second blank.

english/filler-cloze.text: Fill in the blank: 'She was _____ tired that she could not walk.'
english/filler-cloze.sol: 'So...that' is the correct structure to show cause and effect. 'Very' and 'too' do not fit with 'that'.

english/filler-cloze.text: Cloze test: 'The ancient city of Pompeii was _____ by the eruption of Mount Vesuvius. The city remained _____ for centuries until its rediscovery.'
english/filler-cloze.sol: Past tense forms are needed: 'was destroyed' and 'remained buried'.

english/filler-cloze.text: Fill in the blank: 'If I _____ rich, I would travel the world.'
english/filler-cloze.sol: This is a subjunctive (hypothetical) conditional. 'Were' is used for all persons in such constructions (Type 2 conditional).

physics/mechanics.text: A car accelerates uniformly from rest to a speed of 20 m/s in 10 seconds. What is its acceleration?
physics/mechanics.sol: Using v = u + at, with u = 0, v = 20 m/s, t = 10 s. So a = (v - u)/t = (20 - 0)/10 = 2 m/s².

physics/mechanics.text: A force of 50 N acts on a body of mass 10 kg for 5 seconds. Find the change in momentum.
physics/mechanics.sol: Change in momentum = Impulse = F × t = 50 × 5 = 250 kg m/s.

physics/mechanics.text: A body of mass 2 kg is moving with a velocity of 4 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
Two bodies of masses 2 kg and 3 kg have equal kinetic energies. Find the ratio of their linear momenta.
physics/mechanics.sol: KE = p²/2m. For equal KE, p₁²/m₁ = p₂²/m₂. So p₁/p₂ = √(m₁/m₂) = √(2/3) = √2:√3.

physics/mechanics.text: A body is projected vertically upward with velocity 30 m/s. Find the maximum height reached. (g = 10 m/s²)
physics/mechanics.sol: At maximum height, v = 0. Using v² = u² - 2gh, 0 = 900 - 20h, h = 900/20 = 45 m.

physics/thermodynamics.text: A system absorbs 600 J of heat and performs 150 J of work. What is the change in internal energy?
physics/thermodynamics.sol: From first law ΔU = Q - W = 600 - 150 = 450 J.

physics/thermodynamics.text: What is the efficiency of a Carnot engine operating between 227°C and 127°C?
The molar heat capacity at constant volume for a monatomic gas is:
physics/thermodynamics.sol: For a monatomic gas, f = 3 (translational only). Cv = (f/2)R = (3/2)R = ³⁄₂R.

physics/thermodynamics.text: In an adiabatic process, which quantity remains constant?
physics/thermodynamics.sol: In an adiabatic process, no heat exchange occurs (Q = 0). The relation PV^γ = constant holds.

physics/thermodynamics.text: A Carnot engine has efficiency 50%. If the temperature of the sink is 300 K, find the temperature of the source.

physics/optics.text: A convex lens has a focal length of 20 cm. At what distance should an object be placed to obtain a real image of the same size?
physics/optics.sol: For a real image of same size, object distance u = 2f = 40 cm. The image is also at 40 cm on the other side.

physics/optics.text: What is the critical angle for light traveling from glass (n = 1.5) to air (n = 1)?
In Young's double-slit experiment, the fringe width is 0.5 mm when light of wavelength 600 nm is used. What is the fringe width if the wavelength is changed to 400 nm?
A concave mirror of focal length 15 cm forms a virtual image twice the size of the object. Find the object distance.
physics/optics.sol: Magnification m = -v/u = 2 (virtual, erect). v = -2u. Using mirror formula: 1/f = 1/v + 1/u. 1/(-15) = 1/(-2u) + 1/u = (-1 + 2)/2u = 1/2u. So u = -7.5 cm. Magnitude = 7.5 cm.

physics/optics.text: The power of a lens is -2.5 D. Its focal length is:
physics/optics.sol: Power P = 1/f (in meters). So f = 1/P = 1/(-2.5) = -0.4 m = -40 cm. Negative sign indicates concave lens.

physics/electrostatics.text: Two point charges of +3 μC and +6 μC are placed 3 cm apart. Find the force between them. (k = 9 × 10⁹ Nm²/C²)
What is the electric field at a point 20 cm from a point charge of 4 μC?
A 4 μF capacitor is charged to 12 V. Find the charge stored.
If the distance between two charges is halved, the force between them becomes:
physics/electrostatics.sol: F ∝ 1/r². If r becomes r/2, F becomes 1/(r/2)² = 4/r² = 4 times the original.

physics/electrostatics.text: Two capacitors of 2 μF and 3 μF are connected in series. Their equivalent capacitance is:

physics/magnetism.text: A long straight wire carries 10 A current. Find the magnetic field at 5 cm from the wire.
A charge of 2 μC moves with velocity 3 × 10⁵ m/s perpendicular to a magnetic field of 0.4 T. Find the force on the charge.
A solenoid has 500 turns/m and carries 2 A current. Find the magnetic field inside it.
The magnetic flux through a coil of 100 turns changes from 0.02 Wb to 0.06 Wb in 0.4 s. Find the induced emf.
Two parallel wires carry currents in the same direction. The force between them is:
physics/magnetism.sol: Parallel currents in the same direction produce magnetic fields that cause an attractive force between the wires.

physics/modern-physics.text: The work function of a metal is 4.0 eV. What is the threshold frequency? (h = 6.63×10⁻³⁴ Js)
In Bohr's hydrogen atom, the radius of the first orbit is 0.529 Å. What is the radius of the third orbit?
A radioactive substance has a half-life of 4 hours. How much of a 16 g sample remains after 12 hours?
physics/modern-physics.sol: Number of half-lives = 12/4 = 3. Remaining mass = 16 × (1/2)³ = 16 × 1/8 = 2 g.

physics/modern-physics.text: The de Broglie wavelength of an electron accelerated through 100 V is approximately:
Which of the following is not a nucleon?
physics/modern-physics.sol: Nucleons are particles found in the nucleus: protons and neutrons. Electrons orbit the nucleus and are not nucleons.

chemistry/physical-chemistry.text: How many moles are present in 11.2 L of CO₂ gas at STP?
chemistry/physical-chemistry.sol: At STP, 1 mole of any gas occupies 22.4 L. Moles = 11.2/22.4 = 0.5 mol.

chemistry/physical-chemistry.text: For a first-order reaction, the rate constant k = 2.0 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. What is its half-life?
What is the pH of 0.001 M NaOH solution?
chemistry/physical-chemistry.sol: NaOH is a strong base. [OH⁻] = 0.001 = 10⁻³. pOH = -log(10⁻³) = 3. pH = 14 - 3 = 11.

chemistry/physical-chemistry.text: For the reaction N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃, Kc = 16 at 400 K. What is Kc for ½N₂ + ³⁄₂H₂ ⇌ NH₃?
chemistry/physical-chemistry.sol: The second equation is half of the first. When equation is multiplied by ½, Kc' = (Kc)^½ = √16 = 4.

chemistry/physical-chemistry.text: The emf of a cell is 0.59 V at 298 K. For the cell reaction involving n = 2, find ΔG°. (1 F = 96500 C)

chemistry/organic-chemistry.text: The IUPAC name of CH₃CH₂CH₂CHO is:
chemistry/organic-chemistry.sol: The compound has an aldehyde group (-CHO) with 4 carbons, so it is butanal.

chemistry/organic-chemistry.text: Which of the following gives a positive iodoform test?
chemistry/organic-chemistry.sol: The iodoform test is given by compounds with CH₃CO- or CH₃CH(OH)- group. 2-propanol (CH₃CHOHCH₃) has this group.

chemistry/organic-chemistry.text: In SN2 reactions, the product undergoes:
chemistry/organic-chemistry.sol: SN2 involves backside attack by the nucleophile, leading to Walden inversion (inversion of configuration).
Benzene follows Hückel's rule (4n+2 π electrons, n=1 gives 6 π electrons) and is aromatic. The others are not.

chemistry/organic-chemistry.text: Tollens' reagent is used to distinguish between:
chemistry/organic-chemistry.sol: Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal silver nitrate) gives a silver mirror with aldehydes but does not react with ketones.

chemistry/inorganic-chemistry.text: Which of the following is most electronegative?
chemistry/inorganic-chemistry.sol: Electronegativity decreases down the group. Fluorine is the most electronegative element in the periodic table.
XeF₄ has sp³d² hybridization with 2 lone pairs. According to VSEPR theory, the shape is square planar.

chemistry/inorganic-chemistry.text: The coordination number of Fe in K₃[Fe(C₂O₄)₃] is:
chemistry/inorganic-chemistry.sol: C₂O₄²⁻ (oxalate) is a bidentate ligand. Three oxalate ligands give coordination number 3×2 = 6.

chemistry/inorganic-chemistry.text: Which of the following is amphoteric hydroxide?
chemistry/inorganic-chemistry.sol: Al(OH)₃ is amphoteric - it reacts with both acids and bases. NaOH and Ca(OH)₂ are strong bases, Mg(OH)₂ is a weak base.

chemistry/inorganic-chemistry.text: The number of unpaired electrons in Mn²⁺ (atomic number 25) is:
chemistry/inorganic-chemistry.sol: Mn (25): [Ar] 3d⁵ 4s². Mn²⁺: [Ar] 3d⁵. All 5 electrons in d subshell are unpaired (half-filled stability).

chemistry/environmental-chemistry.text: Which gas is primarily responsible for acid rain?
chemistry/environmental-chemistry.sol: SO₂ from industrial emissions dissolves in rainwater to form sulphuric acid, causing acid rain with pH below 5.6.

chemistry/environmental-chemistry.text: The major component of photochemical smog is:
chemistry/environmental-chemistry.sol: Photochemical smog is formed by reactions of NOx and VOCs in sunlight, producing ozone (O₃) and PAN.
Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) measures the amount of oxygen required to decompose organic matter in water. High BOD indicates high organic pollution.

chemistry/environmental-chemistry.text: Which of the following is a secondary pollutant?
chemistry/environmental-chemistry.sol: Peroxyacyl nitrate (PAN) is a secondary pollutant formed by photochemical reactions of primary pollutants (NOx and VOCs).

chemistry/environmental-chemistry.text: The Montreal Protocol is related to:
chemistry/environmental-chemistry.sol: The Montreal Protocol (1987) is an international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out CFCs and other ozone-depleting substances.

biology/cell-biology.text: Which cell organelle is the site of aerobic respiration?
biology/cell-biology.sol: Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell where aerobic respiration occurs, producing ATP through oxidative phosphorylation.

biology/cell-biology.text: Which organelle is responsible for protein synthesis?
biology/cell-biology.sol: Ribosomes, composed of rRNA and proteins, are the site of protein synthesis where mRNA is translated into polypeptide chains.

biology/cell-biology.text: The fluid mosaic model of cell membrane was proposed by:
biology/cell-biology.sol: Singer and Nicolson proposed the fluid mosaic model in 1972, describing the cell membrane as a phospholipid bilayer with embedded proteins.

biology/cell-biology.text: Which of the following is not a part of the endomembrane system?
biology/cell-biology.sol: The endomembrane system includes the ER, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes, and vacuoles. Mitochondria are not part of it.

biology/cell-biology.text: During meiosis, crossing over occurs in which stage?
biology/cell-biology.sol: Crossing over (exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes) occurs during the pachytene stage of prophase I.

biology/genetics-evolution.text: In a monohybrid cross between tall (TT) and dwarf (tt) pea plants, what is the phenotype ratio in F2?
biology/genetics-evolution.sol: In F2 of a monohybrid cross, the phenotypic ratio is 3 (tall) : 1 (dwarf). The genotypic ratio is 1:2:1.

biology/genetics-evolution.text: The DNA molecule is made of two strands that are:
biology/genetics-evolution.sol: DNA strands are antiparallel - one runs 5'→3' and the other runs 3'→5'. This is essential for complementary base pairing.

biology/genetics-evolution.text: In the Hardy-Weinberg equation, what does p represent?
biology/genetics-evolution.sol: In Hardy-Weinberg: p = frequency of dominant allele, q = frequency of recessive allele, p + q = 1.

biology/genetics-evolution.text: Which enzyme synthesizes the leading strand during DNA replication?
biology/genetics-evolution.sol: DNA polymerase III synthesizes the leading strand continuously in the 5'→3' direction toward the replication fork.

biology/genetics-evolution.text: Which of the following is an example of homologous structures?

options.t: Wing of bird and wing of insect
Forelimb of human and wing of bat
Eye of human and eye of octopus
Tail of fish and tail of cat

biology/genetics-evolution.sol: Human forelimb and bat wing are homologous - same basic structure (pentadactyl) modified for different functions, indicating common ancestry.

biology/plant-physiology.text: The end product of photosynthesis is:
biology/plant-physiology.sol: The primary end product of photosynthesis is glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆), which is later converted to starch for storage or sucrose for transport.

biology/plant-physiology.text: Which plant hormone induces fruit ripening?
biology/plant-physiology.sol: Ethylene (C₂H₄) is a gaseous plant hormone that promotes fruit ripening, senescence, and abscission.

biology/plant-physiology.text: The loss of water in the form of water vapor from plant leaves is called:
biology/plant-physiology.sol: Transpiration is the loss of water vapor from aerial plant parts, mainly through stomata in leaves.

biology/plant-physiology.text: Which pigment is essential for photosynthesis?
biology/plant-physiology.sol: Chlorophyll a is the primary photosynthetic pigment that directly participates in light reactions of photosynthesis.
Kranz anatomy (bundle sheath cells surrounding vascular bundles) is a specialized leaf structure found in C4 plants like maize and sugarcane.

biology/human-physiology.text: The cardiac pacemaker is located in the:
biology/human-physiology.sol: The sinoatrial (SA) node, located in the right atrium, is the natural pacemaker of the heart that initiates cardiac impulses.

biology/human-physiology.text: Which enzyme breaks down starch in the mouth?
biology/human-physiology.sol: Salivary amylase (ptyalin) in the mouth breaks down starch into maltose and dextrins.

biology/human-physiology.text: The functional unit of the kidney is:
biology/human-physiology.sol: The nephron is the functional unit of the kidney, responsible for filtration, reabsorption, and secretion.

biology/human-physiology.text: Which hormone regulates blood calcium levels?
biology/human-physiology.sol: Calcitonin (from thyroid) lowers blood calcium by inhibiting bone resorption, while PTH (parathyroid) raises it.

biology/human-physiology.text: The respiratory pigment in human blood is:

csat/comprehension.text: Passage: 'Democracy is not merely a form of government; it is a way of life that requires active participation from citizens. Without an informed and engaged citizenry, democratic institutions become hollow and susceptible to manipulation.' The author's primary argument is that:

options.t: Citizen participation is essential for democracy to function properly
Democratic institutions are naturally resistant to manipulation
Informed citizens are less likely to participate in democracy

csat/comprehension.sol: The passage states that without an informed and engaged citizenry, democratic institutions become hollow and susceptible to manipulation. This implies citizen participation is essential — option b.

csat/comprehension.text: Passage: 'The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence has raised concerns about job displacement. However, history suggests that technological revolutions create new categories of employment even as they render some jobs obsolete.' What can be inferred from the passage?

options.t: AI will definitely cause mass unemployment
Technological change has historically led to new job creation alongside job loss
AI is different from previous technological revolutions
Job displacement due to AI is a new phenomenon

csat/comprehension.sol: The passage states that history suggests technological revolutions create new employment categories even as they obsolete some jobs. So inference: technological change historically creates new jobs alongside job loss — option b.

csat/comprehension.sol: Words like 'stubbornly high', 'disproportionately accrued', and 'struggling' indicate a critical tone towards the outcomes of economic reforms for rural areas.

csat/comprehension.text: Passage: 'The Right to Information Act 2005 has been a landmark legislation in empowering citizens. By providing access to government records, it has enhanced transparency and accountability in public administration.' The main idea of the passage is:

Government records should be kept confidential
RTI Act has reduced corruption completely

csat/comprehension.sol: The passage states that RTI has been landmark in empowering citizens and has enhanced transparency and accountability. The main idea is that RTI Act has empowered citizens and improved transparency — option b.

csat/comprehension.text: Passage: 'Climate change is often presented as an environmental issue, but it is fundamentally a development challenge. Poor communities in developing countries bear the brunt of climate impacts despite contributing the least to greenhouse gas emissions.' What is the author's main point?

options.t: Climate change is only an environmental problem
Developing countries should not be concerned about climate change
Climate change is a development challenge with disproportionate impact on the poor
Rich countries suffer most from climate change

csat/comprehension.sol: The passage argues climate change is fundamentally a development challenge, and poor communities bear the brunt despite contributing the least. Option c best captures this.

csat/logical-reasoning.text: Some doctors are teachers. No teacher is a lawyer. All lawyers are judges. Which of these conclusions definitely follow? I. Some doctors are not lawyers. II. No teacher is a judge.
csat/logical-reasoning.sol: All teachers are not lawyers (no teacher is a lawyer). Some doctors are teachers, so those doctors are also not lawyers → Conclusion I follows. No teacher is a lawyer, but lawyers are judges. Does that mean no teacher is a judge? Not necessarily — the statement says all lawyers are judges, but teachers are not lawyers, so they could still be judges through other means (not necessarily). Actually, every teacher is NOT a lawyer. But the statement 'No teacher is a lawyer' AND 'All lawyers are judges' — we know teachers are not in the lawyer set, but judges set includes lawyers and possibly others. So teachers may or may not be judges. Conclusion II does NOT definitely follow. Let me re-evaluate: I. Some doctors (who are teachers) are not lawyers. Since no teacher is a lawyer, and some doctors are teachers, those specific doctors are not lawyers. So I follows. II. No teacher is a judge — from No teacher is a lawyer, and All lawyers are judges, we cannot conclude teachers are not judges because judges could include non-lawyers. So II does not follow. Only I follows.

csat/logical-reasoning.text: A man walks 5 km East, turns right and walks 3 km, turns right and walks 5 km, turns left and walks 4 km. How far is he from the starting point?
csat/logical-reasoning.sol: Start (0,0). 5 km East → (5,0). Right (South) 3 km → (5,-3). Right (West) 5 km → (0,-3). Left (South) 4 km → (0,-7). Distance = 7 km from start.

csat/logical-reasoning.sol: A and C are sisters (since C is A's sister). A is B's mother. D is C's son. So D and B share a grandmother — they are cousins.

options.t: Ignore it since he is a relative
Report the matter through proper channels

csat/decision-making.sol: Option b is correct — reporting through proper channels upholds integrity, transparency, and the rule of law. Ignoring (a) is unethical. Warning privately (c) bypasses accountability. Resigning (d) avoids responsibility.

csat/decision-making.text: During a disaster, you have limited supplies. Who should receive priority?
csat/decision-making.sol: In disaster management, triage principles dictate that the most critically injured receive priority regardless of status or relationship. Option b follows humanitarian principles and impartiality.

csat/decision-making.text: Your subordinate has been consistently late to work but is otherwise excellent at his job. What is the best course of action?

options.t: Ignore it since his work is good
Give him a written warning immediately
Speak with him privately to understand the reason and find a solution

csat/decision-making.sol: Option c is the most balanced — it addresses the issue directly but empathetically, seeking to understand the root cause before taking punitive action. This maintains team morale while addressing the problem.

options.t: Reject the policy since it harms some people
Implement the policy without considering the affected 20%
Implement the policy with adequate compensation and support for the affected 20%

Respectfully explain your concerns and refuse to approve
Approve but record your objections in the file
Go on leave to avoid the situation

csat/decision-making.sol: Option b is correct — a civil servant must uphold rules and has the right to respectfully disagree. Option c might seem like a compromise but still allows a violation. Options a and d avoid responsibility unethically.

reasoning/puzzles-seating.text: Six persons A, B, C, D, E, F sit in a row facing north. C sits at one end. A sits second to the left of E. B sits to the immediate right of F. D sits third to the right of C. Who sits at the extreme right end?
reasoning/puzzles-seating.sol: C is at one end. D is third to right of C, so C must be at left end, D at 4th position. A is second left of E. B is immediate right of F. Arrangement: C, F, B, D, A, E. D is at extreme right end.

reasoning/puzzles-seating.text: Eight friends sit around a circular table facing the centre. P sits third to the left of T. Q sits to the immediate right of P. R sits between S and U. V sits second to the right of W. Who sits opposite P?
reasoning/puzzles-seating.sol: Place P at some position. T is third right of P (since left means anticlockwise, third anticlockwise = third clockwise from P). Q is immediate right of P. Working around the circle, U sits opposite P.

reasoning/puzzles-seating.text: Seven persons live in a 7-storey building (G to 6). M lives on floor 4. Two persons live between M and N. O lives immediately above P. Q lives on floor 2. R lives above S. Who lives on floor 6?
reasoning/puzzles-seating.sol: M on floor 4. Two between M and N means N is on floor 1 (4-2-1) or 7, but Q on floor 2 so N likely on 1. Q on floor 2. O above P. R above S. Arrangement: G=S, 1=N, 2=Q, 3=P, 4=M, 5=R, 6=O. O lives on floor 6.

reasoning/puzzles-seating.text: In a rectangular table, six persons A-G sit around it, three on each longer side. A faces the person who sits second to the left of B. C sits opposite D. E does not sit adjacent to F. Who sits opposite A?
reasoning/puzzles-seating.sol: Draw rectangle, 3 per side facing centre. C opposite D. A faces second left of B. Using arrangement logic, E is opposite A.

reasoning/puzzles-seating.text: Five friends P, Q, R, S, T in a linear arrangement facing north. R is not at ends. T is to the left of P. Q is to the right of S. R is between S and Q. Who sits in the middle?
reasoning/puzzles-seating.sol: R is not at ends. T left of P. Q right of S. R between S and Q. Order: T, P, S, R, Q. R sits in the middle.

reasoning/inequality.text: Statements: A > B ≥ C = D < E ≤ F. Conclusions: I. A > D II. C < F III. B = D
reasoning/inequality.sol: I. A > B ≥ C = D → A > D ✓. II. C = D < E ≤ F → C < F ✓. III. B ≥ C = D → B ≥ D, not necessarily equal. So only I and II follow.

reasoning/inequality.text: Statements: P ≥ Q > R = S ≤ T < U. Conclusions: I. P ≥ S II. Q > T III. R < U
reasoning/inequality.sol: I. P ≥ Q > R = S → P > S, not P ≥ S. II. Q > R = S ≤ T → Q > R = S ≤ T → Q > S ≤ T, no relation between Q and T. III. R = S ≤ T < U → R < U ✓. Only III follows.

reasoning/inequality.text: Key: A @ B means A > B; A % B means A = B; A # B means A < B; A $ B means A ≥ B; A & B means A ≤ B. Statements: X @ Y $ Z % W # V. Conclusions: I. X > W II. Z ≤ Y
reasoning/inequality.sol: Statements: X > Y ≥ Z = W < V. I. X > Y ≥ Z = W → X > W ✓. II. Y ≥ Z → Z ≤ Y ✓. Both conclusions follow.

reasoning/inequality.text: Statements: M ≥ N > O = P ≤ Q < R. Conclusions: I. M > P II. O < R III. N ≤ Q
reasoning/inequality.sol: I. M ≥ N > O = P → M > P ✓. II. O = P ≤ Q < R → O < R ✓. III. N > O = P ≤ Q → N > O ≤ Q, no relation. I and II follow.

reasoning/inequality.text: Statements: A ≤ B = C > D ≥ E > F. Conclusions: I. A < C II. D > F III. C > E
reasoning/inequality.sol: I. A ≤ B = C → A ≤ C, not necessarily <. II. D ≥ E > F → D > F ✓. III. C > D ≥ E → C > E ✓. II and III follow.

reasoning/data-sufficiency.text: What is the age of A? Statement I: A is 5 years older than B. Statement II: B is 10 years younger than C, and C's age is 30.
reasoning/data-sufficiency.sol: I gives A = B + 5 (1 eq, 2 unknowns). II gives B = C - 10 and C = 30. So B = 20. From I, A = 25. Both together are sufficient.

reasoning/data-sufficiency.text: Is N divisible by 15? Statement I: N is divisible by 5. Statement II: N is divisible by 3.
reasoning/data-sufficiency.sol: 15 = 3 × 5. Both 3 and 5 are coprime. For N to be divisible by 15, it must be divisible by both 3 and 5. Neither alone is sufficient. Together they are sufficient.

reasoning/data-sufficiency.text: Who is the tallest among A, B, C, D? Statement I: A is taller than C and D. Statement II: B is taller than A but shorter than D.
reasoning/data-sufficiency.sol: I: A > C, A > D. II: D > B > A. Combining: D > B > A > C/D. But from I, A > D, and from II, D > A. Contradiction! The statements are inconsistent. Neither is sufficient.

reasoning/data-sufficiency.text: What is the profit percentage? Statement I: SP = ₹1200. Statement II: CP = ₹1000.
reasoning/data-sufficiency.sol: Profit % = (SP - CP)/CP × 100. I alone gives only SP, II alone gives only CP. Together we can compute: (200/1000) × 100 = 20%. Both are needed.

reasoning/data-sufficiency.text: What is the value of x? Statement I: 2x + 3y = 12. Statement II: x - y = 1.
reasoning/data-sufficiency.sol: Two linear equations in two variables from I and II give a unique solution. I alone: infinite solutions (one equation, two unknowns). II alone: infinite solutions. Together: 2x + 3y = 12 and x - y = 1 → solving gives x = 3, y = 2.
